name: Federico Faggin
milestone_by_age_26: Co-designed and built a small experimental electronic computer at Olivetti in 1960-1961 at age 19, leading a team of four technicians.
early_history_summary: Faggin attended a technical high school in Vicenza and joined Olivetti's Electronic R&D Laboratory at age 19, where he co-designed and built a small digital transistor computer. He then earned a laurea in physics summa cum laude from the University of Padua (1965) and joined SGS-Fairchild (1967), where he pioneered MOS metal-gate process technology and designed the first two commercial MOS integrated circuits.
family_context_summary: Born in Vicenza to an intellectual family; father Giuseppe Faggin was a scholar who wrote academic books and translated the Enneads of Plotinus from Greek to Italian.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an academic scholar in philosophy, not directly in technology; the intellectual environment fostered Faggin's early interest in technology but no direct domain transfer is documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: technical institute, Olivetti R&D lab, early computer access, intellectual family
evidence_summary: Faggin grew up in an intellectual household in Vicenza, Italy, where his father was a philosophy scholar. He attended a technical high school and joined Olivetti's R&D lab at 19, where he co-designed and built a small experimental computer with four technicians. He then earned a physics degree summa cum laude from Padua before moving to SGS-Fairchild and then Fairchild Semiconductor in Palo Alto, where he created silicon-gate technology. His early access to Olivetti's R&D lab and rapid mastery of electronics were key advantages.
starting_point: Born to an intellectual family in Vicenza, Italy; father was a scholar who translated classical philosophy texts from Greek to Italian.
current_position: Retired physicist, engineer, and entrepreneur; founder of Synaptics and Foveon; recipient of the National Medal of Technology and Innovation (2009) and Kyoto Prize (1997); resides in the United States.

name: Ángel Cabrera
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first professional golf tournaments at the 1995 Paraguay Open and Colombian Open, marking his emergence as a professional golfer on the South American circuit.
early_history_summary: Cabrera was born in Córdoba, Argentina, to a handyman father and a maid mother. His parents split when he was 3-4 and he was raised by his paternal grandmother. He worked as a caddie at Córdoba Golf Club from age 10, where he met mentor Eduardo Romero, who encouraged him to take up golf at 15 and provided financial assistance. He turned professional at 20 in 1989 and won his first tournaments in 1995 before qualifying for the European Tour in 1996.

name: Go Nagai
